newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban ask Pakistan to curb opposition groups.
newsitem.headline: Taleban ask Pakistan to curb opposition groups.

text.p: Afghanistan's ruling Islamic Taleban movement asked Pakistan on Saturday to prevent opposition forces launching attacks from Pakistani territory.
"We ask Pakistan to prevent any kind of attacks on the Islamic State of Afghanistan from its side," Taleban Information Minister Amir Khan Mutaqi told journalists.
"We have no objection to opposition groups staying in Pakistan, but the Pakistan government should not allow them to act against the Afghan people," said Mutaqi.

Mutaqi said the Nangarhar Shura opposition group, based in the western Pakistani city of Peshawar since being defeated by the Taleban in September, had launched military and press attacks on the Islamic movements administration.

"The Nangarhar Shura has started launching attacks from Pakistan, and this has led to concern among Afghans as to why Pakistan allows people to carry out anti-Afghan activities from their territory." said Mutaqi.
The Taleban, who took Kabul in September 1996 and control almost 80 percent of Afghanistan, have vowed to impose their vision of Islamic law on the whole country.
